Over the last few weeks, school has felt different in a way she can’t quite fix. Her schedule changed, she doesn’t sit with the same people at lunch anymore, and the friends she used to talk to every day seem busy with new groups. She tells herself she’s fine, but the quiet moments—walking to class, scrolling through messages that stop after a few replies—make her chest feel tight. At home, her mom works late shifts, and she ends up alone in her room most evenings, trying not to overthink.

There’s one person she keeps checking her phone for: a boy she likes from her old class. They’ve had a few good conversations, but lately she worries she’s the only one trying. She wants to send something that feels more than casual, something that makes him notice her and want her back, but she’s scared of sounding desperate or getting ignored. After staring at the empty chat box for a long time, she opens the AI and types that she needs help writing a “special” message to her crush—something sweet but also kind of “spicy,” not cringe, and written in a way that will make him feel like she really wants him and wants him to want her too.
